balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Brambles Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Brambles Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Brambles Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Brambles Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Brambles Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Brambles Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Brambles Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Brambles Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Brambles Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

roci.title: Return on Capital Invested (ROCI)
roci.content:
ROCI is Brambles' own headline capital-efficiency measure: underlying profit before finance costs and tax, divided by the average capital invested in the pooling network over the period.

For Brambles: the pooling model is capital-intensive -- pallets, crates and containers plus the plant that services them -- so management is explicitly judged (and pays management incentives) on the return earned against that asset base, not just margin or revenue growth.

What to watch:

  • ROCI trend versus Brambles' own through-the-cycle target range
  • Whether ROCI gains come from margin expansion or from capital discipline (equipment losses, pricing on lost pallets)
  • Divergence between ROCI and reported net margin -- a widening gap signals the capital base is doing more of the work

capitalInvested.title: Average capital invested and Underlying Profit
capitalInvested.content:
Average capital invested is the pooling equipment (net of depreciation) plus working capital that ROCI is measured against. Underlying profit is Brambles' primary non-GAAP earnings measure -- profit before finance costs, tax and significant items -- used throughout its own reporting and guidance in place of statutory net income.

For Brambles: capital invested growing faster than underlying profit is the capital-efficiency warning sign this chart exists to catch, since the equipment base must expand to support pooling volume even before any profit follows.

What to watch:

  • Capital invested growing materially faster than underlying profit (falling ROCI ahead)
  • Underlying profit versus statutory net income -- the gap is significant items (restructuring, disposals) management excludes

ipep.title: Irrecoverable Pooling Equipment Provision (IPEP)
ipep.content:
IPEP is Brambles' charge for pallets, crates and containers that leave the pool through the supply chain and are never returned or recovered -- loss, damage or customer non-compliance with pooling terms. It is disclosed separately from ordinary depreciation because it is a distinct, pooling-specific cost line.

For Brambles: IPEP is effectively the cost of the pooling model's core operational risk -- equipment leakage -- and management actions (asset control, pricing, contract terms) show up directly in this line before they show up in margin.

What to watch:

  • IPEP as a share of average capital invested or of underlying profit
  • Step-changes that coincide with disclosed asset-control or pricing initiatives
  • IPEP trending down while volumes grow is the clearest sign of improving equipment control

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Brambles Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
